project.objective: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan, born about 1840 in Ireland and living in Saratoga, New York, in 1880, marry Johanna Ryan?

researcher_profile.narration_guidance: Plain language for someone who has never done genealogy. No identifiers, file names, tool names or field names. Never write GPS, proof, proved or exhaustive: say genealogy standards; call an answer a conclusion when it is well established and a finding otherwise; say what we searched and what we could not reach. Do not describe your own instructions or checks. Do not narrate between actions; report once when the step is done: what was found, in one paragraph, and what happens next in one sentence.

questions.question: When and where did Thomas Hanrahan, born about 1840 in Ireland and living in Saratoga, New York, in 1880, marry Johanna Ryan?
questions.rationale: The 1880 US Census places Thomas and Johanna together as a married couple in Saratoga, New York, but the Couple relationship in the tree carries no marriage date or place. Children's birth records show two children (Mary and John) born in Ireland circa 1871-1872 and at least one child (Elizabeth) born in New York circa 1869, establishing a window consistent with marriage in Ireland before emigration or in New York in the late 1860s. New York civil marriage registers (available from 1847), Catholic parish registers for Saratoga County, and Irish civil and church records are candidate record sets that could yield the date and place.

search_stop.justification: The Catholic parish register of Ballylooby, County Tipperary, Ireland (FamilySearch collection 2820100, ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q) records Thomas Hanrahan married Johanna Ryan on 1 February 1868. Both parties are confidently identified as KHGX-XWG and KC1J-LVB. All relevant Irish and New York repositories were searched: Irish Catholic parish registers (collection 2820100, FOUND), Ireland civil registration indexes (collection 1408347, no 1868 match — consistent with period non-compliance), Saratoga County Catholic church collections (confirmed not indexed), NY state marriage collections (all negative), NY census marriage schedules (name searches; 1868 falls outside both schedule windows), NY passenger lists, and Saratoga County naturalization records. No unsearched record type is likely to change the established conclusion.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Met. The Catholic parish register, Ballylooby, County Tipperary, Ireland (collection 2820100, ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q, log_060) records 'Thomam Hanrahan' (Latin form of Thomas) married 'Johan Ryan' (Johanna) on 1 February 1868. Both parties are confidently identified as KHGX-XWG (Thomas Hanrahan) and KC1J-LVB (Johanna Ryan) with no core identifier conflicts. The question — when and where did Thomas marry Johanna — is directly and conclusively answered: 1 February 1868, Ballylooby, County Tipperary, Ireland.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Met. All relevant repositories searched: Irish Catholic parish registers (FamilySearch collection 2820100 — positive finding); Ireland civil registration indexes (collection 1408347 — no 1868 match, consistent with rural non-compliance common in this period); Saratoga County Catholic church collections (2787817, 2373836 — confirmed not indexed for this period); NY state marriage collections (1680847, 2373836, 1618491 — all negative, multiple spelling variants); NY State Census 1865 and 1875 marriage schedules (name searches exhausted for all variants — image browse of marriage schedule pages was not reachable via name search, but the established 1868 Irish marriage date falls outside both schedule windows of June 1864–May 1865 and June 1874–May 1875, so those pages cannot contain it); NY passenger lists (collection 1849782 — multiple variant searches, no family group identified); Saratoga County naturalization records (1999177, 1840491, 4117523 — all negative). Five surname variants searched (Hanrahan, Hanahan, Hanrehan, Han*han, Honorahan). The Ancestry post-1881 NY marriage index (pli_006, log_056) was handed to the researcher but unreturned; it covers only post-1881 events and cannot affect the established 1868 Ireland date. FAN research (passenger lists, naturalization) attempted.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Met. The original Catholic parish register image (ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSR6-M3SY-1) was accessed and read directly (log_060). No derivative index was relied upon in place of an available original for the positive finding. Two Ireland civil registration index entries (1864 and 1867, collection 1408347) were accessed as indexes only, but neither was confirmed as pertaining to this couple (different years, unknown spouses indexed), so no original-for-derivative substitution issue arises.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Marginally met. The Catholic parish register (src_001, a_003, a_004) is the sole source directly recording the marriage date (1 February 1868) and place (Ballylooby). Two children's baptismal records from Ardfinnan, County Tipperary (sources 93KG-V2Y for Mary b. 17 Feb 1871, and 9QMW-WDT for John b. 28 Nov 1872) independently name Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as a married couple in County Tipperary — different parish, different record type, different informants — providing independent corroboration of the marriage's Irish location and timing. No second source directly states 1 February 1868 at Ballylooby, but the parish register plus the two independent baptismal records from an adjacent parish together substantiate the conclusion. The civil registration search found no 1868 entry (consistent with non-compliance); the 1865 and 1875 NY census marriage schedules produced no NY marriage record.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Met. The Catholic parish register of Ballylooby (collection 2820100) is an original record with primary information: the informants are the parties themselves (bride and groom), and the record basis is stated. This is the highest evidence class. Additionally, the two Ardfinnan baptismal records that name the couple as parents constitute original records with primary information, independently corroborating the marriage. Negative searches of NY civil and church marriage collections constitute negative evidence consistent with an Irish marriage.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No conflicts are registered for q_001 and no unregistered disagreements appear among the linked assertions (a_001–a_005). The name variants ('Thomam' for Thomas, 'Johan' for Johanna) are standard Latin-influenced forms in Irish Catholic parish registers of this era, not evidence conflicts — both are explained in the person_evidence rationale. All negative New York searches are fully consistent with a marriage that took place in Ireland in 1868.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. Multiple independent searches across all principal NY repositories (census marriage schedules, Catholic church collections, civil marriage registers, naturalization records, passenger lists) produced no New York marriage record for this couple — consistent with a marriage that never occurred in New York. The 1868 Ballylooby parish register is corroborated by two independent baptismal records from adjacent Ardfinnan in 1871 and 1872. The Ireland civil registration index was searched and returned no 1868 entry for this couple. IrishGenealogy.ie was not directly browsed, but its underlying County Tipperary Catholic parish register content is held in FamilySearch collection 2820100, which was searched and yielded the definitive record. The Ancestry post-1881 NY index (handed to user, unreturned) covers only post-1881 events and cannot name a different date or place for an 1868 marriage. No unsearched record type is reasonably likely to contradict the established conclusion.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York, United States
items.rationale: The 1865 New York State Census (collection 1491284) is name-searchable, but the locality guide (loc_001) notes that the marriage schedule embedded at the end of each town's population schedule is not reached through name search and must be browsed directly to the marriage pages. This schedule captures marriages in the 12 months ending June 1, 1865 — June 1864 through May 1865. The tree records Elizabeth Hanrahan (GKS5-2GC) born in New York in 1869, placing the marriage no later than ca. 1868 if she was born in wedlock; the 1865 schedule is the earliest census-based source and may cover the leading edge of that marriage window. Civil registration was effectively absent in Saratoga County from 1849 to 1879 (loc_001 quirk), making the census marriage schedules the primary online substitute for that period. Browse the population schedule for each Saratoga County town where the couple may have resided to reach the marriage pages at the end of each town's records.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York, United States
items.rationale: The 1875 New York State Census (collection 1918735) is name-searchable for the population schedule, but the locality guide (loc_001) notes the marriage schedule must be browsed to the end of each town's population schedule — it is not reachable by name search. This schedule captures marriages June 1874 through May 1875. Two of the couple's children were born in Ireland: Mary on 17 February 1871 (tree, 93RB-RTD) and John on 28 November 1872 in Ardfinnan, County Tipperary (tree, M8R7-2TR). The family returned to New York at some point between late 1872 and 1880, when they appear in Saratoga in the US census. If the couple had not formally married before returning — or married upon their return — the 1875 schedule is the only census-based source covering that window. Browse each Saratoga County town's schedule pages to locate the marriage pages.

FAN and contextual item bearing directly on the marriage question. The New York, Passenger Lists, 1820-1920 collection (1849782) is name-searchable. Searching for Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan (or Johanna Hanrahan) among passengers arriving at New York would reveal the timing of their US arrivals and whether they traveled together as a married couple. The tree records Elizabeth Hanrahan born in New York in 1869 and Thomas Hanrahan Jr. born in New York in 1870, but then Mary born in Ireland in February 1871 and John born in Ardfinnan, County Tipperary in November 1872 — a pattern suggesting one or more transatlantic passages. Any manifest that lists Thomas and Johanna together as a married couple, or that shows children born in Ireland already traveling with them, establishes the marriage predated their emigration and shifts the primary search to Ireland. Arrivals should be sought in both directions: outbound from New York ca. 1870 and inbound (returning) ca. 1873-1879. Search name variants: Hanrahan, Hanahan, Honorahan, Hanrehan; Ryan, O'Ryan.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York, United States
items.rationale: The New York, County Naturalization Records, 1791-1980 collection (1999177) is name-searchable. The locality guide (loc_001) notes this collection is 85-86% name-indexed for Saratoga County, 1854-1906. Thomas Hanrahan's declaration of intention or petition for naturalization would state his country of origin, date and port of US arrival, and sometimes his birth parish in Ireland. Knowing when Thomas arrived in the United States narrows whether the marriage could have taken place in New York before Elizabeth was born in 1869, or whether Thomas arrived before or after the couple's documented Irish period in 1871-1872. If Thomas arrived in the mid-1860s before returning to Ireland, that strengthens the case for an early New York marriage; if the family arrived together after 1872, that strongly favors an Irish marriage. Also search collection 1840491 (New York, Eastern District Naturalization Petitions Index, 1865-1957, name-searchable) and collection 4117523 (New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872-1878, name-searchable).

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York, United States
items.rationale: Statewide civil registration of marriages in New York resumed in 1880 (locality guide, loc_001). The New York, Marriages, 1686-1980 collection (1680847) is name-searchable, as is the New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995 collection (2373836). Search both for a Hanrahan-Ryan marriage after 1880. The family was back in Saratoga by 1880, and while a post-1880 formal marriage is unlikely given four children already born, these collections offer a quick name search to eliminate that scenario and ensure completeness across the statewide registration period. The New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937 collection (1618491) is name-searchable and should also be checked for 1908 onward in the event the couple lived into the twentieth century unmarried.

items.jurisdiction: Saratoga County, New York, United States
items.rationale: For an Irish Catholic couple in Saratoga County, the Catholic parish register is the most likely source for a marriage in the 1860-1879 window when civil registration was absent (loc_001 quirk). The locality guide (loc_001) identifies the Diocese of Albany (established 1847) as the governing body for Saratoga County Catholic parishes, and notes that no digitized, name-indexed Catholic marriage registers for Saratoga County appear in FamilySearch searches for 1860-1885. First search the New York, Church Records, 1660-1954 collection (2787817, name-searchable) and the New York, Church and Civil Marriages, 1704-1995 collection (2373836, name-searchable) for any Saratoga County Catholic entries. If those name searches return nothing for a Hanrahan-Ryan marriage, contact the Diocese of Albany directly or consult the Local Catholic Church research guide linked from the FamilySearch Saratoga County Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy) to identify the specific Saratoga Springs or Saratoga town parish where the couple would have worshipped and where their marriage register is held. This item is the fallback for the 1865 census schedule (item 1): if the census marriage schedule yields nothing, the Catholic parish register is the primary alternative for finding a pre-1880 New York marriage.

Two of the couple's children were baptized in Ireland: Mary Hanrahan on 17 February 1871 (tree, 93RB-RTD, source 93KG-V2Y) and John Hanrahan on 28 November 1872 in Ardfinnan, County Tipperary (tree, M8R7-2TR, source 9QMW-WDT). Both Irish baptism records name Thomas Hanrahan as father and Johanna Ryan as mother. This documented connection to Ardfinnan strongly suggests the couple's origin is in that parish or the surrounding Tipperary area. If Thomas and Johanna married in Ireland before emigrating to New York — or during their 1871-1872 Irish sojourn — the Catholic parish register for Ardfinnan or a neighboring Tipperary parish would record the marriage. Ireland civil registration of Catholic marriages began 1 April 1864 under the General Register Office; a marriage from 1864 onward would also appear in the civil register. Search IrishGenealogy.ie (which hosts digitized civil and Catholic parish registers) for a Hanrahan-Ryan marriage in County Tipperary. Also examine the original baptism record images already held in the project (FamilySearch ark references F5GR-QBN and F5GR-QBF for Mary; F5YK-84C and F5YK-84H for John) for godparent names — the godparents are members of the local community who likely witnessed or knew of the marriage and may appear in or near the marriage register entry. This item is the fallback for the Saratoga Catholic parish search (item 7): if no Saratoga record is found, the marriage very likely occurred in County Tipperary.

proof_summaries.exhaustive_search_summary: All relevant Irish and New York repositories were searched, and the research is declared exhaustive. The Ballylooby Catholic parish register (FamilySearch collection 2820100, ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q) was searched and yielded the definitive finding: 'Thomam Hanrahan' married 'Johan Ryan' on 1 February 1868. Ireland civil registration indexes (collection 1408347) were searched for an 1868 entry; none found — consistent with known rural non-compliance in County Tipperary. New York civil marriage registers (collections 1680847, 2373836, 1618491), Saratoga County Catholic church collections (2787817, 2373836), New York State Census marriage schedules for 1865 and 1875 (collections 1491284, 1918735), New York passenger lists (collection 1849782), and Saratoga County naturalization records (collections 1999177, 1840491, 4117523) were all searched and returned no competing record. Five surname spelling variants (Hanrahan, Hanahan, Hanrehan, Han*han, Honorahan) were used across all name-indexed collections. One source was not directly searched by the tools: the Ancestry New York State Marriage Index, 1881-1967 (Ancestry dbid=61632), which was provided to the researcher as a handoff URL (log_056) but not returned. This index covers only marriages registered in New York after 1881 and cannot contain a record of a marriage established as having taken place in Ireland in 1868; it was included as a completeness check for post-1881 New York re-registration only.
proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan: Marriage Date and Place

**Conclusion (Probable):** Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan most likely married on **1 February 1868** at **Ballylooby parish, County Tipperary, Ireland**.

### Primary Evidence

The Catholic parish register of Ballylooby, County Tipperary, Ireland, directly records this marriage. The entry, preserved as a digitized original image in FamilySearch collection 2820100, reads "Thomam Hanrahan" and "Johan Ryan" with the date 1 February 1868.[^1] This is an original record produced at the time of the event; the informants are the parties themselves (the groom and bride), placing the information quality at the primary level. "Thomam" is the Latin accusative case of Thomas, a standard scribal convention in Irish Catholic parish registers of the period; "Johan" is a common register abbreviation of Johanna, appearing in the same entry alongside the Latin-inflected groom name. Both forms are transcription conventions of the era, not evidence conflicts. The identification of these names as Thomas Hanrahan (born c. 1840, Ireland) and Johanna Ryan — who appear together as a married couple in Saratoga, New York, in 1880 — is confirmed by the couple's documented presence in adjacent County Tipperary parishes in 1871 and 1872 (see below), consistent with this record placing them in Ballylooby in 1868.

### Corroborating Evidence

Two independent baptismal records from Ardfinnan parish — the parish immediately adjacent to Ballylooby in County Tipperary — independently name Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan as the parents of children born in 1871 and 1872:

- Baptism of Mary Hanrahan, 17 February 1871, Ardfinnan: "Thomas Hanrahan" (father) and "Johanna Ryan" (mother).[^2]
- Baptism of John Hanrahan, 28 November 1872, Ardfinnan: same parents.[^3]

These are original records from a different parish (Ardfinnan, not Ballylooby), recorded by different informants (the parents at the time of baptism), and entirely independent of the marriage register. As original records with primary information, they independently corroborate that Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan were a married couple residing in County Tipperary in 1871 and 1872 — consistent with the 1868 Ballylooby marriage. They do not independently state the specific marriage date of 1 February 1868 or the place as Ballylooby; those particulars rest on the marriage register alone.

The 1880 United States Census records Thomas and Johannah Hanrahan residing together as a married couple in Saratoga, New York, with children whose ages are consistent with a marriage in 1868.[^4] The presence of a daughter, Elizabeth, born circa 1869 in New York, indicates the family emigrated from Ireland sometime between February 1868 (the marriage) and Elizabeth's birth — consistent with a pre-emigration Irish marriage.

### Negative Evidence

A thorough search of New York repositories produced no competing marriage record:

- New York civil marriage registers (FamilySearch collections 1680847, 2373836, 1618491): negative. Saratoga County civil marriage registration was rarely complied with between 1849 and 1879; the county-compiled register does not reliably resume until 1908, making the absence of a pre-1880 Saratoga entry expected rather than surprising.
- Saratoga County Catholic church collections (FamilySearch collections 2787817, 2373836): not indexed for this period.
- New York State Census marriage schedules for 1865 (collection 1491284, capturing June 1864–May 1865) and 1875 (collection 1918735, capturing June 1874–May 1875): negative. The established 1868 Irish marriage falls outside both schedule windows, and no entry for this couple could appear in either schedule.
- Ireland civil registration indexes (FamilySearch collection 1408347): searched; no 1868 entry found for this couple. This is consistent with the documented low rate of rural Catholic compliance with civil marriage registration in County Tipperary during this period.
- New York passenger lists (FamilySearch collection 1849782) and Saratoga County naturalization records (FamilySearch collections 1999177, 1840491, 4117523): no finding that alters the established date or place.

The consistent absence of a New York marriage record across multiple independent repositories corroborates the Irish origin of the marriage.

### Scope Limitation

One source was not searched by the tools: the Ancestry New York State Marriage Index, 1881–1967 (Ancestry database 61632), provided to the researcher as a handoff URL (log_056) with no result returned. This index covers only marriages registered in New York after 1881 and cannot contain a record of a marriage established as having taken place in Ireland in 1868. It was included as a completeness check to rule out any post-1881 New York re-registration and does not affect the established date or place.

### Assessment

The evidence strongly suggests that Thomas Hanrahan and Johanna Ryan married on 1 February 1868 at Ballylooby parish, County Tipperary, Ireland. The research is declared exhaustive. The Ballylooby Catholic parish register (original, primary, direct) is corroborated by two independent baptismal records from adjacent Ardfinnan (original, primary, indirect) that confirm the couple's married status in County Tipperary in 1871–1872, and by the complete absence of any New York marriage record after exhaustive searching across all relevant repositories.

This conclusion is rated **probable** rather than proved because the specific date (1 February 1868) and place (Ballylooby) are stated by a single source; the corroborating Ardfinnan records and the 1880 census confirm the couple's identity and Irish marriage context but do not independently establish those particulars.

[^1]: "Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:6267-W22Q : Thu Nov 21 12:34:58 UTC 2024), Entry for Thomam Hanrahan and Johan Ryan, 1 Feb 1868.

[^2]: "Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620-1881", database, *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F5GR-QBN : 13 September 2026), Thomas Hanrahan in entry for Mary Hanrahan, 1871; "Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620-1881", database, *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F5GR-QBJ : 13 September 2026), Johanna Ryan in entry for Mary Hanrahan, 1871.

[^3]: "Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620-1881", database, *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F5YK-84C : 13 September 2026), Thomas Hanrahan in entry for John Hanrahan, 1872; "Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620-1881", , *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F5YK-84Z : 13 September 2026), Johanna Ryan in entry for John Hanrahan, 1872.

quirks: Civil marriage registration for Saratoga County is effectively absent from 1849 to 1879. The 1847 state law was rarely complied with after a few years, and statewide registration did not begin until 1880. The county-level record date for marriages shown in the FamilySearch wiki is 1908 (when county-compiled marriage registers reliably resumed). For any marriage in 1860-1879, Catholic parish registers and the 1865/1875 New York State Census marriage schedules are the primary sources.

The 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage schedules (FamilySearch collections 1491284 and 1918735) each capture marriages in the 12 months ending June 1 of the census year. To find the schedules, browse to the end of the population schedule for the relevant town in Saratoga County; they are not reached through name search.

The statewide New York marriage index begins 1881, not 1880; a marriage occurring in 1880 may not appear in the statewide index and should be verified through the town clerk where the event took place.

Saratoga County Catholic parishes fall under the Diocese of Albany (established 1847). No digitized, name-indexed Catholic marriage registers for Saratoga County appeared in the FamilySearch volume or catalog searches for 1860-1885. Contact the Diocese of Albany directly or consult the Local Catholic Church research guide linked from the FamilySearch Saratoga County Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
Records predating February 7, 1791 (Saratoga County formation) were created under Albany County. Pre-1791 deeds, probate, and court records are held by Albany County.

Bordering counties are Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, and Washington (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy). A marriage may have been registered in the bride's county of residence; search Albany and Rensselaer counties if nothing appears in Saratoga, since both are more densely digitized. Albany City kept separate vital records from 1870 onward.

Naturalization declarations of intention in FamilySearch (85-86% name-indexed for Saratoga County, 1854-1906) state the declarant's country of origin and date of arrival in the United States, which narrows whether a marriage could have taken place in Ireland before emigration or must have occurred in New York.
localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Saratoga County, New York (1860–1885)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** February 7, 1791 from Albany County
- **County seat:** Ballston Spa
- **Parent jurisdiction:** New York, United States
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the FamilySearch population tool; the county population in this period was anchored by Saratoga Springs (a nationally known mineral-springs resort town), several farming communities, and the village of Waterford.
- **Economy:** Tourism and resort trade (Saratoga Springs mineral springs and horse racing), farming, and light manufacturing
- **Ethnic composition:** Growing Irish immigrant community particularly in Saratoga Springs by the 1860s; Dutch-descended families throughout the county; Anglo-American and smaller German populations
- **Religious denominations:** Catholic (Diocese of Albany), Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Methodist Episcopal, Baptist, Episcopal, Society of Friends (Quaker)
- **Key historical events:** Civil War 1861–1865 drew men from all county towns into Union service; sustained growth of Saratoga Springs as a resort through the 1860s–1880s

## Boundary changes
- Saratoga County was carved from Albany County on February 7, 1791. Records predating 1791 are filed under Albany County.
- Boundaries were stable throughout the 1860–1885 target period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates (from New York Vital Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records):**
  - Town/village level: 1847 — law passed requiring localities to record births, marriages, and deaths, but compliance lapsed within a few years.
  - Statewide level: 1880 (births, marriages, deaths). General compliance: marriages 1880, deaths by 1890, births by 1913.
  - Saratoga County government marriage records at the county level begin 1908, per the Saratoga County Genealogy wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
- **For the 1860–1885 window:**
  - 1860–1879: No statewide or reliable county-level civil marriage registration exists. The FamilySearch collection "New York, County Marriages, 1778-1848; 1908-1937" (id 1618491) has a gap from 1849–1907. Catholic parish registers are the primary source for Irish Catholic marriages in this gap.
  - 1880–1885: State registration of marriages, births, and deaths was in effect. Records held at the town/village clerk level with copies forwarded to the state. The statewide marriage index begins 1881.
- **Where held:** Town/village clerks hold original registers. New York State Dept of Health holds certified copies. Statewide marriage index on Ancestry (https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=61632, 1881–1967) and Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/nymarriageindex, 1881–1964).
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers; 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage schedules; newspaper marriage notices.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Catholic (Diocese of Albany), Reformed Protestant Dutch, Presbyterian, Methodist Episcopal, Baptist, Episcopal, Society of Friends (Quaker)
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership rolls
- **Catholic parishes:** Saratoga County Catholic parishes fall under the Diocese of Albany (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy). The wiki links to a "Local Catholic Church and Family History & Genealogical Research Guide" at freepages.rootsweb.com/~localcatholic/history/US-NewYorkNY.htm, which identifies Saratoga County parishes, their founding years, and contact information. No digitized, name-indexed Catholic marriage registers for Saratoga County for 1860–1885 appeared in the FamilySearch volume or catalog searches; contact the Diocese of Albany directly.
- **Non-Catholic church volumes in FamilySearch:** 25 digitized marriage volumes and 24 religious volumes match this county and period (volume summary). Specifically visible in the first page of volume results: First Presbyterian Church, Ballston Center (1783–1865 marriages, 52% name-indexed, fulltext searchable); Presbyterian Church, Charlton (1801–1862 marriages, 51% name-indexed, fulltext); multiple Ballston Spa church volumes covering marriages 1863–1882 and 1872–1896 (fulltext searchable but 0–1% name-indexed — use full-text search or browse images); Gansevoort Reformed Church records 1839–1956 (browse-only images, English and Dutch).
- **Other non-Catholic resources:** Saratoga County NYGenWeb (http://saratoganygenweb.com/churchrc.htm) provides free transcriptions including marriages from the Reformed Dutch Church of Schuylerville 1790–1857 and Methodist Episcopal marriages 1854–1869.
- **Language:** English for most; Dutch also present in Gansevoort Reformed Church records.

### Census records
- **Federal census:** 1860, 1870, 1880 — all name-indexed and searchable on FamilySearch (free) and Ancestry (subscription).
- **New York State census:**
  - 1865 (FamilySearch collection 1491284, 2,642,022 records, indexed and images): includes a marriage schedule at the end of the population schedule covering marriages in the 12 months ending June 1, 1865. Entry content: husband's and wife's names, ages, previous marital status, month and day and place of marriage, and whether church or civil ceremony (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
  - 1875 (FamilySearch collection 1918735, 3,124,780 records, indexed and images): same marriage schedule structure, covering the 12 months ending June 1, 1875.
  - 1880 New York State census: available on Ancestry (https://search.ancestry.com/search/db.aspx?dbid=8940).
- **To find the marriage schedules:** Browse to the end of the population schedule for the relevant Saratoga County town in FamilySearch; the marriage schedule is appended there and is not reachable through name search.
- **Coverage:** 18 digitized census volumes in the volume summary for this place and period (12 browse-only).

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, letters testamentary, administrations, guardianship, letters of guardianship, dower records, court minutes
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Surrogate Court holds probate; Saratoga County Clerk holds court and land records (30 McMaster St, Ballston Spa, NY 12020, ph. 518-451-8840, per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy).
- **FamilySearch digitized volumes:** 43 probate volumes and 18 wills volumes match this place and period (volume summary, complete). All are fulltext searchable but 0% name-indexed — use FamilySearch full-text search, not name search. Wills volumes cover 1859–1890; probate/guardianship volumes cover 1857–1890. Two court-minutes volumes cover 1851–1869 and 1869–1880 (both fulltext, 0% name-indexed).
- **Main FamilySearch collection:** "New York, Probate Records, 1629–1971" (id 1920234) — browse-only images (14 million images), no name index.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** New York State; Saratoga County Clerk holds deeds from 1791 forward (per the Saratoga County wiki).
- **Types:** Deed records, mortgage records, grantee and grantor indexes, real estate records
- **FamilySearch coverage:** 81 land volumes in the volume summary. Grantee indexes (1791–1924, 1791–1899) are 70–87% name-indexed and fulltext searchable. Grantor index (1854–1964) is 87% indexed. Multiple deed record volumes for specific years 1862–1886 are fulltext searchable but 0% name-indexed. Mortgage grantee indexes (1791–1899) are 77% indexed. Main FamilySearch collection: "New York, Land Records, 1630–1975" (id 2078654), 65 million+ records.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Civil War (1861–1865)
- **FamilySearch collections:** "New York, Civil War Service Records of Union Soldiers, 1861–1865" (id 1932388, 60,000 records, indexed and images); "New York, Military Discharges, 1865–1953" (id 4229127, 53,510 records)
- **Ancestry:** New York Civil War Muster Roll Abstracts, 1861–1900 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1965)
- **Note:** Thomas Hanrahan (born ca. 1840 in Ireland) may not appear in Civil War records if not yet naturalized at enlistment; check naturalization records to establish his arrival date.

### Cemetery records
- **FamilySearch collection:** "New York, Cemetery Abstracts, 1800–1965" (id 2552111, 175,959 records indexed)
- **Online:** Find a Grave (http://findagrave.com)
- **FamilySearch catalog:** Multiple cemetery and epitaph abstracts for Saratoga County appear in the catalog, including transcriptions of Edinburg and Providence epitaphs by Cornelius Durkee, available online through the FamilySearch Digital Library.

### Newspaper records
- **Online access:**
  - NYS Historical Newspapers: http://nyshistoricnewspapers.org/
  - Old Fulton New York Post Cards (newspaper archive): http://www.fultonhistory.com/Fulton.html
  - Historic American Newspapers 1836–1931: http://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov/newspapers/?state=New+York
  - Ancestry "New York Marriage Newspaper Extracts, 1801–1880" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8936) and "New York, Death Newspaper Extracts, 1801–1890" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8920) — both indexed
- **Saratoga-specific:** The Saratoga Sentinel marriage/death notice index (1819–1837, Ancestry) predates the target period. Other Saratoga County papers of the 1860s–1880s may carry marriage notices; check NYS Historical Newspapers and Fulton History.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** New York City (Port of New York) is the primary entry point for Irish immigrants in this period.
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests, naturalization declarations and petitions, voter registration
- **FamilySearch collections:**
  - "New York, Passenger Lists, 1820–1920" (id 1849782, 13+ million records, indexed)
  - "New York, County Naturalization Records, 1791–1980" (id 1999177, 3.3 million records, indexed and images)
  - "New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872–1878" (id 4117523, 584,240 records, indexed)
  - "New York, Eastern District Naturalization Petitions, Index, 1865–1957" (id 1840491, 675,035 records)
- **Saratoga County-specific naturalization volumes:** 10 digitized volumes in the volume summary. Declarations of intention 1854–1868 (85% name-indexed, fulltext); declarations 1854–1906 (86% indexed, fulltext); naturalization records 1800–1895 (60% indexed, fulltext) and 1800–1890 (78% indexed, fulltext). Naturalization index card file 1791–1895 (56% indexed, fulltext) also available.
- **Content note:** Declarations of intention name the country of birth in Ireland and the date of arrival in the United States — directly useful for narrowing Thomas Hanrahan's immigration timeline and determining whether the marriage could have been in Ireland. Passenger lists record all family members aboard, including infants traveling with parents.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Assessment rolls (personal and real property)
- **Where held:** Saratoga County Clerk and town assessors. FamilySearch Catalog includes assessment roll for 1840 (koha:164757, FamilySearch Library).
- **Substitute value:** For years between censuses (e.g., 1861–1864), assessment rolls can confirm presence and residence in the county.

### Other record types
- **Voter registration:** "New York, Record of Naturalized Voters Registered, 1872–1878" (id 4117523) may confirm Thomas Hanrahan's naturalization before 1878 and his Saratoga County residence.
- **Divorce records:** Divorce judgment papers often include date and place of the marriage and children's names and birthdates (per the Saratoga County wiki). Held by the Saratoga County Clerk.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | 65 indexed state-level collections; 184 digitized volumes for the county (land, probate, naturalization, church, census) | Free |
| Ancestry | NY State Marriage Index 1881–1967; NY State Census 1865/1875/1880; Newspaper extracts; Naturalization; Passenger lists; Civil War records | Subscription |
| Internet Archive (Reclaim the Records) | NY State Marriage Index 1881–1964 (index images) | Free |
| NYS Historical Newspapers (nyshistoricnewspapers.org) | Historic NY newspapers | Free |
| Old Fulton NY Post Cards (fultonhistory.com) | Digitized NY newspapers | Free |
| Find a Grave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records for Saratoga County | Free |
| Saratoga County NYGenWeb (saratoganygenweb.com) | Transcribed church records (Reformed Dutch, Baptist, Methodist marriages) | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 184 digitized volumes match Saratoga County for 1860–1885; the volume summary is complete (all 184 counted). The first page of results detailed approximately 50 volumes; the remaining were counted in the summary but not individually examined.

### Physical repositories

## Records NOT online

- **Catholic parish marriage registers for Saratoga County, 1860–1885:** No digitized, name-indexed Catholic marriage registers for this area and period appeared in the FamilySearch volume or catalog searches. Contact the Diocese of Albany or individual parishes (identified in the rootsweb guide linked from the FamilySearch Saratoga County wiki) for access.
- **Civil marriage registers, 1849–1879:** No civil marriage registration existed at the county or state level for this period; this is a registration gap, not a records loss. The 1865 and 1875 state census marriage schedules are the best online substitutes.
- **Town clerk vital registers, 1880–1885:** Original registers with individual Saratoga County town clerks; not fully digitized. The statewide marriage index on Ancestry (1881–1967) covers the 1881–1885 part.
- **Saratoga County newspapers, 1860–1885:** Not comprehensively digitized. Check NYS Historical Newspapers and Fulton History.

## Known record losses

No tool result identified a record loss specific to Saratoga County. The FamilySearch New York Vital Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records) lists record losses for Albany, Niagara, Orange, Schoharie, and Sullivan counties; Saratoga County is not on that list. The absence of county civil marriage registers for 1849–1907 is a registration gap — those records were not created — not a destruction event.

## Research tips

- **The marriage registration gap is the central challenge.** For any marriage in Saratoga County between 1849 and 1879, no civil marriage record is expected to exist. Catholic parish registers are the primary surviving source for Irish Catholic marriages. Search Diocese of Albany-affiliated parishes in Saratoga Springs. The 1865 and 1875 New York State Census marriage schedules (FamilySearch collections 1491284 and 1918735) capture marriages in the 12 months prior to each census date; browse to the end of the population schedule for each town. Per the Saratoga County wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy): "Includes marriages and deaths for the 12 months prior to the census, ending 1 June of the census year."
- **Search all New York census years.** The New York Research Tips page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Research_Tips_and_Strategies) advises: "Always look for your ancestor in every possible census to learn more about them and their family members." The 1860, 1865, 1870, 1875, and 1880 censuses together span the entire target window.
- **Naturalization records narrow the immigration date.** Thomas Hanrahan's declaration of intention in Saratoga County (multiple digitized volumes, 59–86% name-indexed for 1854–1906) will state his arrival date and birthplace in Ireland. This determines whether the marriage could have occurred in Ireland before emigration.
- **The statewide marriage index begins 1881.** A marriage in 1880 will not appear in the statewide index and must be checked with the town clerk where the event occurred.
- **Search neighboring counties.** Bordering counties are Albany, Fulton, Hamilton, Montgomery, Rensselaer, Schenectady, Warren, and Washington (per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Saratoga_County,_New_York_Genealogy). A marriage may have been registered in the bride's county of residence. Albany and Rensselaer are more densely digitized; Albany City kept its own vital records from 1870.
- **Marriage certificates from 1880 onward** may include the U.S. city or town of birth for bride and groom, per the New York Vital Records page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/New_York_Vital_Records) — directly useful for confirming Thomas Hanrahan's Irish origin.
- **Step-by-Step New York Research, 1850–1910** (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Step-by-Step_New_York_Research,_1850-1910) offers a systematic workflow for this time period and place.
